problem: Five registered retrieval interventions failed on the same seven outcome-selected cases, and six prompt-only bridge analogues had already failed on another three-case cluster. Continuing to select mechanisms from those cases would overfit the development evidence and leave the project's benchmark story dependent on small slices.
simplest_baseline: Run the frozen Pi v10 Query-Aware Progressive Disclosure policy once, sequentially, on all 175 development questions. Change no search policy, prompt, model, retriever, call cap, or output budget; use the resulting valid traces only to measure the broader failure distribution.
hypothesis: The frozen policy will produce 175 valid predictions with at least 168 schema-complete answers, zero tool-transport failures, zero output-budget overshoot, and at least 30 Judge-wrong cases suitable for a broader mutually exclusive bad-case taxonomy. No accuracy threshold is used to promote a mechanism from this profiling run.
changed_mechanisms: evaluation scope from an outcome-selected seven-case cluster to the frozen 175-question development partition
anti_claim: This changes evaluation scope, not model parameters or intrinsic capability. Because the policy was selected using development data, the result is profiling rather than fresh confirmatory evidence.

framework_comparisons.current_gap: DeerFlow explicitly treats sub-agents as an optimization. A broader failure distribution is required before claiming that parallel latency, specialization, or context isolation is the limiting factor here.
Its public evaluation spans 100 tasks and its older supervisor-researcher implementation is documented as less performant. The immediate deficit is measured scope, not missing role labels.
Its breadth-oriented topology should be compared only after the frozen single-Agent policy has a full development error profile under an auditable cost and trace contract.
Concurrency is a latency intervention. It remains deferred until the broader profile shows independent branch omission or serial latency rather than shared retrieval failure.
